# Coinbase AI Agents Debut to Automate Crypto Trading and Portfolio Management

Coinbase has officially launched "Coinbase for Agents," a new tool designed to connect AI agents directly to user accounts. This development allows systems to trade cryptocurrencies, make payments, and manage portfolios on behalf of users within predefined guardrails. The move signals a significant step into the world of AI-driven finance, as major players like [Coinbase](https://cointelegraph.com/news/coinbase-launches-tool-letting-ai-agents-make-payments-and-trade-crypto?utm_source=rss_feed&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=rss_partner_inbound) and others are rapidly developing AI agent financial tooling.

According to Coinbase, the tool gives AI agents access to both financial information and transaction capabilities. This enables them to analyze portfolios and execute actions within limits set by the user. The platform is available through a Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration for web-based AI assistants like ChatGPT and Claude, as well as a command-line interface for developers using tools such as Hermes Agent, Anthropic’s Claude Code, and OpenAI Codex. The goal is to make crypto management more autonomous, reducing the need for constant manual oversight from users. As [reported](https://decrypt.co/370835/coinbase-tool-ai-agents-trade-crypto-make-payments), this could include tasks like allocating funds to reward programs or setting up recurring buys.

## The Vision for Autonomous Finance

Coinbase's vision extends beyond simple automation. The company aims to position AI agents as a primary way for people to interact with the internet and their finances. Lincoln Murr, head of AI product at Coinbase, stated, "We believe agents are no longer a niche developer curiosity, but really a primary way people interact with the internet." This forward-looking perspective highlights the potential for AI to revolutionize how investors approach the crypto market.

### Practical Applications and Use Cases

The new tool opens up a range of practical applications for users. For example, an agent could be instructed to execute a dollar-cost averaging (DCA) strategy for Ethereum at the most optimal time of day. The agent would analyze 30 days of hourly price data to identify historical lows, then set up a recurring buy at that specific time. This level of automation can help investors implement complex strategies with minimal effort. Other potential use cases include portfolio rebalancing, cash management, and even purchasing premium datasets to inform trading decisions. The system is designed to operate within isolated portfolios with controls like spending limits and trade-size restrictions.

### Introduction of Coinbase Advisor

Alongside the agent tool, Coinbase has introduced "Coinbase Advisor," an AI-powered financial advisor registered with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC). This integration provides users with AI-driven trade guidance and recommendations directly within the Coinbase app. The advisor can offer insights on trades and help users navigate the complexities of the crypto market, further enhancing the platform's capabilities for both new and experienced traders.

## Industry-Wide Push for AI Integration

Coinbase is not alone in its push towards AI-driven finance. The entire industry is seeing a wave of innovation in AI agent financial tooling. This trend underscores a broader shift towards leveraging artificial intelligence to create more sophisticated and user-friendly financial products. The rapid development in this area suggests that AI will play an increasingly central role in the future of crypto and traditional finance.

### Competitors and Ecosystem Growth

Several other major players are making significant strides in this space. For instance, stablecoin issuer Circle recently launched tools that allow AI agents to use wallets and make programmable payments. Circle's CEO, Jeremy Allaire, predicts that billions of AI agents will be using stablecoins within the next five years. Similarly, crypto payments firm MoonPay has launched MoonAgents, a desktop application that enables AI to interact with wallets, token swaps, and other blockchain services. Even traditional finance giants like Mastercard are getting involved, with the introduction of "Agent Pay for Machines," a platform for autonomous machine-to-machine payments.

### A Word of Caution

Despite the excitement surrounding these developments, there are reasons to be cautious. A recent study from Pantera Capital and Stanford University examined over 925,000 agentic token holders and found that while agent treasuries saw paper gains of $30 million, the token holders themselves collectively lost $191.7 million. The researchers also noted that many of the projects studied did not show clear evidence of autonomous trade execution, with a "substantial share" being little more than basic API integrations. These findings serve as a reminder that the technology is still in its early stages and that investors should remain vigilant.

The launch of Coinbase AI agents and Coinbase Advisor represents a major milestone in the integration of artificial intelligence with cryptocurrency trading. These tools offer the promise of simplifying portfolio management and providing traders with powerful new capabilities. As the industry continues to innovate, the role of AI in finance is set to expand, with companies like Circle and Mastercard also making significant investments in the space. However, it is crucial for users to remain aware of the risks and limitations of these emerging technologies, as highlighted by recent academic research.

'Coinbase for Agents' is a new tool from Coinbase that allows AI agents to connect to user accounts to trade crypto, make payments, and manage portfolios within user-defined limits.

Yes, Coinbase Advisor is an AI agent registered with the SEC and CFTC that provides AI-powered trade guidance and recommendations directly within the Coinbase app.

Use cases include automated strategies like dollar-cost averaging, portfolio rebalancing, recurring investments, and cash management.

Yes, a recent study indicated that users of some AI agent systems have incurred significant financial losses, and the autonomy of these agents is sometimes questionable.
